facts.fact: The page states that the global Dynamic Ad Insertion market is growing from USD 7.2 billion in 2023.
facts.quote: growing from **USD 7.2 billion in 2023** to a projected **USD 29.8 billion by 2033**.

facts.fact: The page says that around 2020 there was a big push for server-side insertion to improve how ads were delivered.
facts.quote: Around **2020**, we saw a big push for server-side insertion to improve how ads were delivered.

facts.fact: The page says that by 2022 the conversation in dynamic ad insertion had shifted toward data privacy and delivering relevant ads while respecting user consent.
facts.quote: By **2022**, the conversation had shifted to focus more on data privacy and how to deliver relevant ads while respecting user consent.

facts.fact: Server-Side Ad Insertion (SSAI) stitches video and ads into one unified stream on the server before it reaches the viewer's device.
facts.quote: Here, the video content and the ads are stitched together into one single, unified stream on the server. This happens _before_ the video even begins its journey to the viewer's device.

facts.fact: The page states that SSAI is good at getting around ad blockers because ads are baked directly into the video stream.
facts.quote: Because the ads are baked directly into the video stream, SSAI is good at getting around ad blockers

facts.fact: The page states that Client-Side Ad Insertion (CSAI) is more vulnerable to ad blockers than SSAI.
facts.quote: It's more vulnerable to ad blockers and can sometimes lead to that dreaded buffering wheel

facts.fact: The page says in Client-Side Ad Insertion the video player makes a separate call to an ad server to fetch an ad when an ad break comes up.
facts.quote: the video player itself makes a separate call to an ad server to grab an ad.

facts.fact: The page says the ad decisioning engine scans what it knows about the viewer, such as general location or device type, and picks an ad from its inventory in a fraction of a second.
facts.quote: In a fraction of a second, the decisioning engine scans what it knows about the viewer (maybe their general location or the type of device they're using) and picks the best possible ad from its inventory.

facts.fact: The page states that DAI lets publishers offer hyper-targeted ad slots that command higher CPMs than generic placements, without giving a numeric CPM figure.
facts.quote: DAI lets publishers offer hyper-targeted ad slots (based on location, viewing habits, or demographics) that command much higher prices (CPMs) than generic, spray-and-pray placements.

facts.fact: The page was published on 2025-11-17.
Third-party research cited by the page (Grand View Research via marketresearch.com) projects app-based ad delivery within dynamic ad insertion to grow at a 12.8% CAGR through 2030.
facts.quote: app-based ad delivery is projected to grow at a **12.8% CAGR** through 2030

facts.fact: The page defines impressions as how many times an ad was seen, and reach as how many unique people saw it.
facts.quote: **impressions** (how many times your ad was seen) and **reach** (how many unique people saw it)

facts.fact: The page states that most platforms let advertisers set daily or campaign-wide spending caps.
facts.quote: Most platforms let you set daily or campaign-wide spending caps, so there are no surprises.

facts.fact: The page describes GDPR as the General Data Protection Regulation, the standard for data protection and privacy for anyone with an audience in the European Union.
facts.quote: **GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation):** The big one for anyone with an audience in the European Union.

facts.fact: The page describes CCPA as the California Consumer Privacy Act, which gives California residents significant control over their personal information.
facts.quote: **CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act):** This gives California residents significant control over their personal information

facts.fact: The page states that shoppable video format availability depends on the platform and placement.
facts.quote: Availability depends on the platform and placement.

facts.fact: Dynamic ad insertion (DAI) is technology that places ads into streaming content in real time rather than having them pre-embedded.
facts.quote: Dynamic ad insertion (DAI) is technology that places ads into streaming content in real-time rather than being pre-embedded.

facts.fact: Adwave Digital, per the page, many DAI platforms operate on flexible CPM models, where CPM means cost per thousand impressions.
facts.quote: many operate on flexible models like **CPM (cost per thousand impressions)**.

facts.fact: According to the page, Platforms like Adwave Digital have moved away from massive upfront commitments, so a small business can start with a small budget.
facts.quote: Platforms like **Adwave Digital** have moved away from massive upfront commitments.

facts.fact: The page states that Server-Side Ad Insertion (SSAI) stitches ads into the video stream before it reaches the viewer, which the page says mostly sidesteps ad blockers.
facts.quote: This server-side approach also neatly sidesteps most ad blockers, which is important for making sure your ads are seen during those can't-miss live moments.

facts.fact: The page says DAI enables targeting by demographics, interests, and behaviors rather than only by the channel a viewer is watching.
facts.quote: You can reach specific audiences based on demographics, interests, and behaviors rather than just whoever happens to be watching a particular channel.
